mcp.description: Scan any website or MCP server for agent readiness: 0-100 score, a fix per failing check. Free.

mcp.name: app.vercel.agent-svg-registry/mcp
mcp.description: Search SVG metadata and buy licensed commercial SVG exports for coding agents.

reading.body:
Vercel hosts two MCP servers that equip AI agents to evaluate and extend their own capabilities: one scores websites and servers for agent compatibility, the other enables agents to license visual assets for code generation.

The agentready server represents infrastructure for agent self-assessment. An agent can run it against itself or a target system and receive a scored readiness report with specific fixes. This is distinct from most AI tooling, which assumes agents operate within fixed constraints. Instead, Vercel is publishing a diagnostic layer that lets agents identify what they can and cannot do before attempting tasks.

The agent-svg-registry server solves a concrete problem: agents that generate UI code need visual assets, and licensing creates friction. By making SVG purchase discoverable and transactional within agent workflows, Vercel lowers the cost of agents generating production-ready interfaces. Both servers point to the same pattern: removing friction that otherwise forces agents to stop, escalate to humans, or produce incomplete work.

Neither server addresses compute, buildings, or power directly. Both assume that agent infrastructure already exists and that the constraint now is workflow completion within that infrastructure. The data does not reveal how widely these servers are used, whether they are internally focused on v0's own agent capabilities, or critical infrastructure for the broader agent ecosystem.

profile_text.body:
Vercel is a for-profit startup founded in 2015 and headquartered in San Francisco, CA. The company develops web infrastructure and developer tooling, and its own site presents v0 as a collaborative AI assistant designed to help users design, iterate, and scale full-stack web applications.

v0 is Vercel's primary AI product, categorized as a coding and developer tool with a focus on UI generation. The site describes it as enabling full-stack web app development through an AI-assisted workflow, positioning Vercel within the growing space of AI-powered development environments.

The held facts note 187 legal exposure entries tied to California, though no specific cases are recorded. Vercel also has two MCP server listings: one that scans websites or MCP servers for agent readiness and returns a scored report with recommended fixes, and one that provides SVG metadata search and licensed commercial SVG exports for coding agents.
